texts.at-0001: Round money only with round_money Round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
texts.at-0002: Raise BillingError with snake_case codes Signal domain validation failures by raising BillingError(code, detail) with a snake_case code such as "invalid_state", "invalid_quantity" or "negative_amount", matching ledgerly/payments.py.
texts.at-0003: Normalize amounts with to_money before storing Convert any incoming amount through ledgerly.money.to_money (and compare against ZERO) before storing it on a model, so unit_price is always a Decimal.
texts.at-0004: Reject bools and non-int quantities When validating integer quantities, explicitly exclude bool (isinstance(quantity, bool)) since True/False are ints in Python, and require quantity > 0.
texts.at-0005: Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ledgerly.clock.ensure_utc` before comparing or doing arithmetic; it raises `BillingError` for naive or non-datetime values. Follow the pattern in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`.
texts.at-0006: Period math mirrors subscriptions module Billing period arithmetic uses `timedelta(days=sub.period_days)` from `sub.started_at`, as already done in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`; reuse that pattern rather than inventing new period logic.

item.title: Use money helpers for all amounts
item.content: Convert every monetary input with `to_money` and round results with `round_money` from `ledgerly/money.py`; never use floats or raw `Decimal` quantize. `to_money` rejects floats with `BillingError("float_amount")`.
